statement: A mid-2026 claimed decipherment of Linear A by self-taught AI/ML engineer Tom Di Mino (first reported ~30 July 2026, expanded ~13 August 2026), identifying the underlying language as Semitic with a 40-42 sign readings, a 408-508-word lexicon, and ~443 proposed translations built using AI-assisted text organization and comparative work against Semitic inscriptions, is under review by linguists at Rutgers and Cambridge, has no peer-reviewed publication, and no independent confirmation. Di Mino has no formal linguistics training, and the field treats the claim with explicit "calibrated skepticism" given a long history of failed amateur Linear A decipherment claims. This claim does NOT change decipherment_status from UNDECIPHERED and should not be pre-encoded as resolved.

sources.citation: GreekReporter.com coverage of the Di Mino Linear A claim, 30 Jul 2026 and 13 Aug 2026.
AI Insiders, "An AI Engineer Says He Decoded Linear A. Here Is What He Actually Showed."

does_not_demonstrate: That Linear A has been deciphered (this remains an unpublished, unreviewed, contested claim as of the current date)
notes: Included specifically as a live example of the "definitely says X" popular-overclaim risk this project is built to catch — do not let this claim's existence read as endorsement.
